details: Minneapolis Federal Reserve President Neel Kashkari indicated on Wednesday that markets anticipate more interest rate hikes than Fed officials currently project, citing persistent inflation and a resilient job market. Separately, Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller supported a 50-basis-point rate increase for December or a signal for a January hike, driven by a sustained rise in core Consumer Price Index (CPI). These hawkish remarks reinforce expectations for tighter monetary policy, which typically creates a less favorable environment for risk assets like cryptocurrencies.
title: Fed Officials Signal Continued Rate Hikes Amid Inflation Concerns

details: Bitcoin continued its downward trend on Thursday, extending losses for the seventh consecutive week and hovering near multi-month lows. This decline is attributed to a combination of factors, including the anticipation of further interest rate hikes, which make non-yielding assets less appealing. November has seen significant outflows from US-listed spot Bitcoin and Ethereum ETFs, approaching $3 billion and $1 billion respectively, highlighting a sustained withdrawal of institutional capital from crypto investment products.
title: Bitcoin Extends Losses as ETF Outflows and Macro Pressures Mount

details: A recent selloff in artificial intelligence (AI) stocks, exacerbated by the "AI debt crisis" and the resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, has fueled a broader risk-off sentiment in financial markets. This increased investor caution is putting additional pressure on higher-risk assets, including cryptocurrencies, as funds are reallocated to safer investments.
title: AI Stock Selloff Contributes to Broader Risk-Off Sentiment

details: The European Central Bank (ECB) is reportedly close to discussing and potentially deciding to double the minimum reserve requirement for banks at its December meeting. This move, which would cut excess liquidity by €175 billion and save the ECB €4.4 billion annually, could put additional pressure on money markets. While primarily aimed at reducing costs for the ECB, tighter liquidity conditions in the Eurozone could have broader implications for global financial markets and risk appetite.
title: ECB Reportedly Considering Doubling Minimum Bank Reserves in December
